Recently watched Coolie, I actually liked this movie. 
1. Had a good blend of characters. 
2. Reminisce Loki Ana's Maanagaram handling of its actors and screenplay. 
3. Some noteworthy stunts. Upendra Sir was brought in well with a superb BGM. 
4. Colour themes used in movie apt. Saturated choices in hostel blends.
5. Shruthi proves she is organic to any given screenplay.
6. Simon, Kalyani, Dahaa all rocked. Dayal sizzled.
7. Loki fans will understand his style of movie making and I feel Coolie was justified @Loki style.
8. Anirudh Ana songs and BGM fit well.
9. Devaraj looked awesome for me. 

Some afterthought for improvement. 
1. The very idea of roasting bodies could have been substituted with a "scientific" concept as the handling of the devices looked very straight forward and don't convince why the thugs could not have done it themselves. 
2. Though may appear cliche, uniting Preethi with Devaraj would have been better. Or at the very least, silently suggest that Preethi knew Deva was her father.
3. The chemistry between Deva and Rajashekar didn't quite click. Perhaps more visuals and screentime required.
4. When we talk about action sequences, I would appreciate some gun sequences using heavy machinery i.e. Kaithi style. It would have packed a punch. 
5. These mid story flash backs i.e. young Simon disrupts movie's momentum, either its best in the beginning or a short recap like post credit scenes. 

Just some thoughts, Loki Ana and team, vazhtugal. Thumbs up from me. Loved the movie. ❤

Anne franks early life shows what kind of person she was before the war changed everything.
Anne Frank was born on June 12, 1929, in Frankfurt, Germany. She lived with her mom, dad, and older sister Margot. When Anne was still young, her family moved to Amsterdam because life in Germany was becoming dangerous for Jewish families. Anne was a normal kid in many ways, but she was also very thoughtful and loved to write. She liked sharing her feelings and ideas, which is one reason her diary became so important later. In her diary, Anne wrote, “I hope I will be able to confide everything to you” (Frank). This shows that writing helped her express herself and deal with her thoughts. Anne’s early life was important because it helped shape the girl the world would later remember
One of anne franks biggest achievement was her diary witch helped people understand what life was like during the holocaust .

Her diary shared her thoughts, fears, and hopes during a very hard time. Anne once wrote, “Paper has more patience than people” (Frank). This shows that writing helped her feel understood when she could not talk freely to others. She also wrote, “I want to go on living even after my death” (Frank). That quote is important because her words really did live on after she died. Anne’s diary became one of the most well-known books from World War II, and it helped many people learn from her story
Anne frank had a big inpact on the world because her diary helped people understand the pain of the holocaust in a personal way.
Even though Anne Frank was just a young girl, her words ended up reaching millions of people. Her diary showed what life was like for a Jewish family hiding during World War II. It helped people see that the Holocaust was not just history, but something real that happened to real families. Anne once wrote, “In spite of everything, I still believe that people are really good at heart” (Frank). This quote is important because it shows how hopeful she stayed, even during such a terrible time. Her diary has been read in schools all over the world and has taught many people about courage, hope, and kindness. Because of Anne Frank, people still remember what happened and why it should never happen again.

Imagine being promised a blockbuster thunderbolt, but what you get is more like your neighbor’s firecracker that fizzles out before the “Happy Independence Day” echo fades. That’s Coolie.

The film bills itself as a gritty union-leader-turned-hero saga—but with a star-studded cast and booming budget of ₹350–400 crore, it feels like the masala was forgotten in the pot. It tries to juggle plot threads like a clown juggling fire torches—light-hearted in intent, but mostly leaving you singed and underwhelmed.

First half? Highlands of spice. Rajinikanth tries to carry the weight like a seasoned port worker, and the opening scenes almost stick. But post-interval, it's more of a slow slog through the suppression of logic. The crime plot? Less Underworld noir, more Underwhelming snore. The action sometimes feels like an overzealous trailer edit—flashy but hollow.

Worse, the screenplay keeps introducing twists like they’re freebies at a roadside stall—one too many, and you just lose the taste. Even Soubin Shahir tries to inject fun, but ends up stranded like a fan missing a firecracker’s final burst. 

Punchy dialogue? More like punch-drunk confusion. Music by Anirudh is flashy, sure—but feels a bit like trying to jazz up bland food with too much garnish. No matter how shiny the decorations, you’re still eating stale dishes.

In short: Coolie is a high-budget, star-loaded can that wants to explode—but forgets the fuse.

Rating: 0.5/5 – A film so overhyped it feels like being promised firework, but getting a damp matchstick instead.
